data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism contains a sweeping, unsupported universal empirical claim: 'Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour.' This assertion is presented as established fact yet the target provides no premises, no derivation (the derivation array is empty), no formalization, no simulation, and no references to support it. The claim makes two extraordinary sub-claims: (1) that there exist 'previously studied systems of this kind' that faced 'identical structural constraints,' and (2) that none of them 'exhibited this behaviour.' Neither the systems nor their structural constraints nor the behavioural comparison are identified anywhere in the target. This is a bare universal generalization functioning rhetorically to make the Popperian position appear uniquely anomalous, but it has no evidential or argumentative foundation. A claim of universal scope about all previously studied systems cannot be smuggled into a mechanism paragraph without any support; it is a genuine substantive fault.
